method: A nonlinguistic Polya urn, seed 31128: sequentially write one existing invented token sampled uniformly from all previous draws, or invent a new numbered token with probability 300/(300+number of preceding tokens). Write the token number in base six using a,o,d,e,i,y, with q and r as fixed delimiters. The parameter, encoding, and seed are fixed in advance; no manuscript text, vocabulary, or target entropy is used. Lines of nine are packaging only. A growing preferential-attachment lexicon generates heavy-tailed frequencies without semantics. This differs from the previously submitted independent fair-dice control; it tests memory and cumulative reinforcement. The same fixed-seed sample was submitted against F-031 and F-024. The urn has global memory and never observes page boundaries; this tests whether its reinforcement alone suffices for page reuse, without a page-specific vocabulary rule.
